task.name: An issue is closed when a referencing PR merges, so a symptom bug is recorded resolved before its symptom is observed to stop
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

An issue is closed when a referencing pull request merges, regardless of whether
the reported symptom has been observed to stop. For a symptom bug this records an
unverified claim as a resolved one.

Concretely, on 2026-07-29 PR #2062 merged into `release/v0.13` carrying a fix for
#2047 — forward-port CI runs held at `action_required` because branch pushes
authenticated as the Actions token rather than the App. The PR body used the
phrase `Fixes #2047`, and #2047 was closed `COMPLETED` on merge with the comment
"Closed by merged PR #2062."

The symptom had not been observed to stop, and still has not. The defect occurs on
the `synchronize` event — a force-push to an *existing* forward-port PR. The merge
that closed the issue produced only the `opened` path, which was never broken. The
fix is deployed and plausible; the reported symptom remains untested. The issue
reads as verified anyway.

This is not a workflow misfire. It closed exactly the issue the PR body named, by
design. The problem is that merging a change and confirming a symptom stopped are
different facts, and only one of them was established.

## Expected behavior

Closing an issue asserts that the problem it reports no longer occurs. Where a
project's own process distinguishes shipping a change from confirming the reported
symptom is gone — and this one does, requiring that reviewers verify symptom
resolution rather than implementation correctness alone — automation that closes on
merge collapses that distinction and converts an unverified change into a recorded
resolution. A closure driven by a code event rather than by an observation should
either be withheld for the class of issue whose resolution is defined by an
observation, or be recorded in a way that does not claim more than the merge
established.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** a symptom bug is closed `COMPLETED` at merge time while
  the behavior it reports is still unobserved, leaving no open record that
  verification is outstanding.

- **Evidence:** `.github/workflows/close-on-merge.yml` triggers on
  `pull_request: types: [closed]` for `branches: ["release/**"]` (lines 19-21),
  gated to merged PRs only (line 30). Lines 44-47 extract issue numbers following
  a closing keyword (`close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?`) from the PR body.
  Lines 54-60 close every referenced issue whose state is `OPEN`, commenting
  "Closed by merged PR #N". No step consults the issue's type, its diagnosis
  state, or any verification signal. The workflow's own header comment (lines
  14-16) states the intended contract: "A story issue closes when the story merges
  to its base branch."

- **Ruled out:** not a keyword-matching error — the pattern matched the phrase the
  PR body actually used. Not a permissions or event-scoping problem; the workflow
  is event-scoped to the single PR in the payload and behaved as documented. Not
  specific to hand-authored PRs, since the same path runs for any merged PR
  referencing an issue with a closing keyword.

- **Confirmed cause:** closure is triggered by the merge event alone. The workflow
  has no notion of whether an issue's resolution is defined by a code change or by
  an observed behavior, and applies the same closing action to both.

- **Affected code path:** `.github/workflows/close-on-merge.yml`, the closing-keyword
  extraction and close loop.

- **Fix-success criterion:** a merged pull request referencing an issue whose
  resolution is defined by an observed behavior does not leave that issue recorded
  as resolved before the behavior has been observed, and an operator can tell from
  the issue's state alone that verification is outstanding.

## Notes

The immediate instance was caught by hand and cost nothing. The exposure is that it
is silent by construction: nothing distinguishes an issue closed because the
symptom stopped from one closed because a referencing PR merged, so an unverified
closure is indistinguishable from a verified one after the fact.

handoff.summary: Modified .github/workflows/close-on-merge.yml so that a merged PR referencing an issue with the `bug` label no longer closes that issue automatically. Bug issues are left OPEN, get a new `verify-symptom` label (created idempotently via `gh label create --force`), and receive a comment naming the merging PR and explaining that the symptom has not yet been observed to stop. Non-bug issues (stories, enhancements) continue to close on merge exactly as before, preserving the existing story-close contract. Added tests/test_close_on_merge_workflow.py, which extracts the actual shell step from the YAML and runs it under bash with a stubbed `gh` CLI, covering: bug issue stays open + labeled + commented; non-bug issue still closes; already-closed issue is skipped regardless of label; label-create call happens.

commits.message: fix(ci): don't auto-close bug issues on merge before symptom verified

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A merged pull request referencing an issue whose resolution is defined by an observed behavior does not leave that issue recorded as resolved before the behavior has been observed
acceptance_criteria.notes: Bug-labeled issues are no longer closed by the merge event; they stay OPEN with a verify-symptom label until closed by an actual verification step (manual or future automation).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An operator can tell from the issue's state alone that verification is outstanding
acceptance_criteria.notes: The issue remains OPEN and carries the verify-symptom label, so `gh issue list --label verify-symptom` or the issue's own label list makes the outstanding verification visible without reading history/comments.

handoff.story_deviations: Chose to distinguish issue type via the pre-existing `bug` label (used by bug_report.md) rather than adding new issue-type metadata, since it already exists and matches the spec's framing of 'the class of issue whose resolution is defined by an observation.' Chose to leave the issue open + label + comment (rather than withhold closing entirely with no signal), per the spec's second allowed option: 'be recorded in a way that does not claim more than the merge established.'

handoff.summary: Fixed the gate failure: an E501 (line too long) violation in tests/test_close_on_merge_workflow.py's docstring, plus a ruff-format issue on the WORKFLOW path assignment. Ran ruff check and ruff format --check on src/ and tests/ — both clean. Ran the full test suite (make gate's pytest step); 6572 passed, 38 skipped, 17 failed. Investigated the 17 failures individually: all are PermissionError from multiprocessing.SemLock or mktemp under /var/folders — sandbox restrictions on this machine, confirmed unrelated to my change since they occur in test_cut_rc_isolation.py, test_sprint_lock.py, and test_sprint_reexec_collision.py (none of which import or touch the files I modified), and reproduce identically in isolated single-test runs outside xdist. No functional change was made beyond the original fix; only the lint/format issue was addressed.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
